instruction: How is the egress capacity calculated for a security access turnstile lane with a clear passage width of 32 in. or more?
input: Component: Security Access Turnstile Lane, Condition: Clear Passage Width 32 in. or More
output: According to NFPA 101, any security access turnstile lane configuration providing a clear passage width of 32 in. (810 mm) or more shall be given an egress capacity as calculated in accordance with the code.

instruction: What are the dimensional requirements for the marking stripe on exit stair treads?
output: According to NFPA 101, the marking stripe shall be not more than 1/2 in. (13 mm) from the leading edge of each step, shall not overlap the leading edge by more than 1/2 in. (13 mm) down the vertical face, and shall have a minimum horizontal width of 1 in. (25 mm) and a maximum width of 2 in. (51 mm).

instruction: What are the maximum dimensions for an interior exit discharge through a buffer or foyer?
output: According to NFPA 101, the depth from the exterior of the building shall be not more than 10 ft (3050 mm), and the length shall be not more than 30 ft (9.1 m).

instruction: What is the additional width required at the outer side of a spiral stairway?
output: According to NFPA 101, at the outer side of the spiral stairway, an additional 10 1/2 in. (265 mm) of width shall be provided clear to the other handrail, and this width shall not be included as part of the required egress capacity.

instruction: What is the area threshold for requiring a designated means of egress path within normally unoccupied building service equipment support areas in buildings protected throughout by an approved, supervised automatic sprinkler system?
output: According to NFPA 101, a designated means of egress path shall be provided within the normally unoccupied building service equipment support area where the area exceeds 90,000 ft² (8370 m²) in buildings protected throughout by an approved, supervised automatic sprinkler system.

instruction: What is the capacity credit for each turnstile meeting specific criteria?
input: Condition: Turnstiles approved by authority having jurisdiction and meeting criteria
output: According to NFPA 101, each turnstile shall be credited for a capacity of 50 persons, provided that such turnstiles meet all of the following criteria: they freewheel in the egress direction when primary power is lost, and freewheel upon manual release by an employee assigned in the area; they are not given credit for more than 50 percent of the required egress width; and they are not in excess of 39 in. (990 mm) in height.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for determining the required clear floor area of an elevator lobby for evacuation?
output: According to NFPA 101, the elevator lobby clear floor area shall accommodate, at 3 ft² (0.28 m²) per person, at least 50 percent of the occupant load of the floor area served by the lobby.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for fire escape stairs serving 10 or fewer occupants?
input: Component: Fire Escape Stairs, Condition: Serving 10 or Fewer Occupants
output: According to NFPA 101, the capacity factor for fire escape stairs serving 10 or fewer occupants is 1/2 inch (13 mm) per person, if access by door; 1 inch (25 mm) per person, if access by climbing over windowsill; if winders or ladder from door, 10 persons; if bottom balcony, 5 persons; if both, 1 person.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for level components and ramps in high-hazard contents areas?
input: Occupancy: High-Hazard Contents, Component: Level Components and Ramps
output: According to NFPA 101, the egress capacity for high-hazard contents areas shall be based on 0.4 in./person (10 mm/person) for level components and ramps.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for level components in all other occupancies?
output: According to NFPA 101, the capacity factor for level components in all other occupancies is 0.3 in. (7.6 mm) per person.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for level components in board and care occupancies?
output: According to NFPA 101, the capacity factor for level components in board and care occupancies is 0.4 in. (10 mm) per person.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for level components in nonsprinklered health care occupancies?
output: According to NFPA 101, the capacity factor for level components in nonsprinklered health care occupancies is 0.6 in. (15 mm) per person.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for replacement fire escape stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the capacity factor for replacement fire escape stairs is 1/2 inch (13 mm) per person, if access by door; 1 inch (25 mm) per person, if access by climbing over windowsill.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for stairways and ramps in all other occupancies?
output: According to NFPA 101, the capacity factor for stairways and ramps in all other occupancies is 0.2 in. (5 mm) per person.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for stairways and ramps in high-hazard contents occupancies?
output: According to NFPA 101, the capacity factor for stairways and ramps in high-hazard contents occupancies is 0.4 in. (10 mm) per person.

instruction: What is the capacity factor for stairways and ramps in nonsprinklered health care occupancies?
output: According to NFPA 101, the capacity factor for stairways and ramps in nonsprinklered health care occupancies is 0.5 in. (13 mm) per person.

instruction: What is the clearance used when measuring travel distance around corners or obstructions?
output: According to NFPA 101, when measuring travel distance, a 12 in. (305 mm) clearance from corners or obstructions shall be used.

instruction: What is the egress capacity for a security access turnstile lane with a clear passage width of less than 32 in.?
input: Component: Security Access Turnstile Lane, Condition: Clear Passage Width Less Than 32 in.
output: According to NFPA 101, any security access turnstile lane configuration providing a clear passage width of less than 32 in. (810 mm) shall be given an egress capacity of 50 persons.

instruction: What is the fire protection rating required for doors in an occupant evacuation shaft system?
input: Component: Occupant Evacuation Shaft System Doors
output: According to NFPA 101, the doors shall have a fire protection rating of not less than ¾ hour.

instruction: What is the height range for existing required handrails on stairs?
input: Component: Existing required handrails on stairs
output: According to NFPA 101, existing required handrails shall be not less than 30 in. (760 mm), and not more than 38 in. (965 mm), above the surface of the tread, measured vertically to the top of the rail from the leading edge of the tread.

instruction: What is the horizontal extent of roof construction required for protection beneath outside stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, roof construction shall extend horizontally to each side of the stair for not less than 10 ft (3050 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum allowable floor level change at door openings that requires beveling?
output: According to NFPA 101, raised thresholds and floor level changes in excess of 1/4 inch (6.3 mm) at door openings shall be beveled with a slope not steeper than 1 in 2.

instruction: What is the maximum allowable floor level difference for existing buildings where a door discharges to the outside?
input: Condition: Existing building, door discharging to outside or exterior balcony
output: According to NFPA 101, in existing buildings where the door opening discharges to the outside or to an exterior balcony or exterior exit access, the floor level outside the door opening shall be permitted to be one step lower than that of the inside, but shall be not more than 8 inches (205 mm) lower.

instruction: What is the maximum allowable variation in floor elevation on both sides of a door opening?
output: According to NFPA 101, the elevation of the floor surfaces on both sides of a door opening shall not vary by more than 1/2 inch (13 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum change in elevation that requires beveling for walking surfaces in the means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, changes in elevation exceeding 1/4 in. (6.3 mm), but not exceeding 1/2 in. (13 mm), shall be beveled with a slope of 1 in 2.

instruction: What is the maximum clear floor area for an area of refuge that does not require a smokeproof enclosure when created by a horizontal exit?
input: Condition: Area of Refuge Created by Horizontal Exit
output: According to NFPA 101, the smokeproof enclosure shall not be required for areas of refuge that are more than 1000 square feet (93 square meters) of clear floor area and that are created by a horizontal exit.

instruction: What is the maximum collapsing force for revolving door assemblies not used as a component of a means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, revolving door assemblies not used as a component of a means of egress shall have a collapsing force not exceeding 180 lbf (800 N) applied at a point 3 in. (75 mm) from the outer edge of the outer wing stile and 40 in. (1015 mm) above the floor.

instruction: What is the maximum common path of travel in mechanical equipment rooms, boiler rooms, and furnace rooms when the building is sprinklered?
input: Occupancy: Mechanical Equipment Rooms, Boiler Rooms, Furnace Rooms, Condition: Sprinklered
output: According to NFPA 101, a common path of travel not exceeding 100 ft (30 m) shall be permitted in mechanical equipment rooms, boiler rooms, and furnace rooms, provided that the building is protected throughout by an approved, supervised automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 9.7 and no fuel-fired equipment is within the space.

instruction: What is the maximum cross slope for new ramps?
output: According to NFPA 101, new ramps shall have a maximum cross slope of 1 in 48.

instruction: What is the maximum dead end length on an exterior exit access balcony?
output: According to NFPA 101, dead ends on the exterior exit access balcony shall not exceed 20 ft (6100 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum distance between intermediate rails for guards?
output: According to NFPA 101, the distance between intermediate rails, measured at right angles to the rails, shall not exceed 21 in. (535 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum distance from all portions of the required egress width for handrails on new stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, for new stairs, handrails shall be provided within 30 in. (760 mm) of all portions of the required egress width.

instruction: What is the maximum distance from the door frame for mounting an exit sign on or adjacent to an exit door?
input: Component: Exit Sign, Condition: Exit Door
output: According to NFPA 101, for exit doors, the exit sign shall be mounted on the door or adjacent to the door, with the nearest edge of the sign within 4 in. (100 mm) of the door frame.

instruction: What is the maximum distance from the floor for supply air entry and the maximum height for the top of the exhaust register in a vestibule?
output: According to NFPA 101, supply air shall enter the vestibule within 6 in. (150 mm) of the floor level, and the top of the exhaust register shall be located not more than 6 in. (150 mm) below the top of the trap.

instruction: What is the maximum distance from the nearest sign for exit access?
output: According to NFPA 101, exit access signs shall be located not more than 100 ft (30 m) from the nearest sign.

instruction: What is the maximum distance from the wall for perimeter floor demarcation lines?
output: According to NFPA 101, perimeter floor demarcation lines shall be placed within 4 in. (100 mm) of the wall and extend to within 2 in. (51 mm) of the markings on the leading edge of landings.

instruction: What is the maximum distance that a conforming side-hinged swinging door assembly must be located from a revolving door?
input: Component: Side-Hinged Swinging Door Assembly, Condition: Adjacent to Revolving Door
output: According to NFPA 101, each revolving door assembly shall have a conforming side-hinged swinging door assembly in the same wall within 10 feet (3050 mm) of the revolving door.

instruction: What is the maximum force required to collapse revolving door wings into a book-fold position?
output: According to NFPA 101, revolving door wings shall be capable of being collapsed into a book-fold position when a force not exceeding 130 lbf (580 N) is applied to the wings within 3 in. (75 mm) of the outer edge.

instruction: What is the maximum force required to fully open any door leaf manually in a means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, the forces required to fully open any door leaf manually in a means of egress shall not exceed 30 lbf (133 N) to set the leaf in motion, and 15 lbf (67 N) to open the leaf to the minimum required width.

instruction: What is the maximum force required to operate a horizontal-sliding door assembly in the direction of door leaf travel?
output: According to NFPA 101, the force required to operate a horizontal-sliding door assembly in the direction of door leaf travel shall be not more than 30 lbf (133 N) to set the door leaf in motion and not more than 15 lbf (67 N) to close the door assembly or open it to the minimum required width.

instruction: What is the maximum force required to operate a special-purpose horizontally sliding accordion or folding door in the direction of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, the force required to operate the door in the direction of travel is not more than 30 lbf (133 N) to set the door in motion and is not more than 15 lbf (67 N) to close the door or open it to the minimum required width.

instruction: What is the maximum force required to operate a special-purpose horizontally sliding accordion or folding door when a perpendicular force is applied?
output: According to NFPA 101, the door is operable using a force of not more than 50 lbf (222 N) when a force of 250 lbf (1100 N) is applied perpendicularly to the door adjacent to the operating device, unless the door opening is an existing special-purpose horizontally sliding accordion or folding exit access door assembly serving an area with an occupant load of fewer than 50.

instruction: What is the maximum height above the finished floor for perimeter wall demarcation lines?
output: According to NFPA 101, perimeter wall demarcation lines shall be placed on the wall with the bottom edge of the stripe not more than 4 in. (100 mm) above the finished floor.

instruction: What is the maximum height between landings for existing ramps?
output: According to NFPA 101, existing ramps shall have a maximum height between landings of 12 ft (3660 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum height between landings for replacement fire escape stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the maximum height between landings for replacement fire escape stairs is 12 feet (3660 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum height difference between the floor level and a door opening serving spaces that are not normally occupied?
output: According to NFPA 101, where doors serve spaces that are not normally occupied, the floor level shall be permitted to be lower than that of the door opening but shall be not more than 8 in. (205 mm) lower.

instruction: What is the maximum height for a guard?
output: According to NFPA 101, a guard shall be permitted to exceed 38 in. (965 mm), but shall not exceed 42 in. (1065 mm), measured vertically to the top of the guard.

instruction: What is the maximum height for a releasing mechanism for locks and latches on a door leaf?
output: According to NFPA 101, the releasing mechanism for locks and latches shall be located not more than 48 in. (1220 mm) above the finished floor.

instruction: What is the maximum height for approved turnstiles that turn freely in the direction of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, approved turnstiles not exceeding 39 in. (990 mm) in height that turn freely in the direction of egress travel shall be permitted where revolving door assemblies are permitted in Chapters 11 through 43.

instruction: What is the maximum height for the top of an emergency exit symbol above the finished floor?
output: According to NFPA 101, the top of the emergency exit symbol shall not be higher than 18 in. (455 mm) above the finished floor.

instruction: What is the maximum height for thresholds at door openings?
output: According to NFPA 101, thresholds at door openings shall not exceed 1/2 inch (13 mm) in height.

instruction: What is the maximum height of risers for stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the maximum height of risers is 8 in. (205 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum height of the lowest rung of a fire escape ladder above the surface beneath it?
output: According to NFPA 101, the lowest rung of any ladder shall not be more than 12 in. (305 mm) above the level of the surface beneath it.

instruction: What is the maximum horizontal dimension for beveling or rounding at tread nosings?
output: According to NFPA 101, at tread nosings, such beveling or rounding shall not exceed 1/2 in. (13 mm) in horizontal dimension.

instruction: What is the maximum horizontal distance from an unprotected building opening that triggers inclusion of travel to finished ground level?
output: According to NFPA 101, where any part of an exterior exit is within 10 ft (3050 mm) of horizontal distance of any unprotected building opening, the travel distance to the exit shall include the length of travel to the finished ground level.

instruction: What is the maximum horizontal distance from the edge of the egress opening for egress markings?
output: According to NFPA 101, egress markings shall be located at a horizontal distance of not more than the required width of the egress opening, as measured from the edge of the egress opening intended for designation by that marking to the nearest edge of the marking.

instruction: What is the maximum horizontal force to actuate a cross bar or push pad on a power-operated door?
input: Component: Power-Operated Door, Condition: Emergency Breakout Mode
output: According to NFPA 101, a horizontal force not to exceed 15 lbf (66 N) shall actuate the cross bar or push pad such that the door leaf opens and latches.

instruction: What is the maximum landing dimension in the direction of travel for a straight run stair?
output: According to NFPA 101, landings shall not be required to exceed 48 in. (1220 mm) in the direction of travel, provided that the stair has a straight run.

instruction: What is the maximum lateral separation between alternating treads?
output: According to NFPA 101, the alternating treads shall not be laterally separated by a distance of more than 2 in. (51 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum level of access opening above the floor for replacement fire escape stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the maximum level of access opening above the floor for replacement fire escape stairs is not over 12 inches (305 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum mounting height for devices on egress door assemblies from individual living units and guest rooms?
output: According to NFPA 101, devices on egress door assemblies from individual living units and guest rooms of residential occupancies shall be mounted at a height not exceeding 48 in. (1220 mm) above the finished floor.

instruction: What is the maximum mounting height for existing security devices on egress doors?
output: According to NFPA 101, existing security devices permitted by 7.2.1.5.3.4, other than automatic latching devices, shall be located not more than 60 in. (1525 mm) above the finished floor.

instruction: What is the maximum number of persons allowed in a subdivided space without a door leaf or opening in the folding partition?
input: Condition: Subdivided space used under adult supervision
output: According to NFPA 101, a door leaf or opening in the folding partition is not required provided the subdivided space is used by not more than 20 persons at any time.

instruction: What is the maximum occupancy for spaces where fire escape ladders are permitted?
output: According to NFPA 101, fire escape ladders are permitted in means of egress from towers, elevated platforms around machinery, boiler rooms, or similar spaces subject to occupancy not to exceed three persons.

instruction: What is the maximum occupant load served by alternating tread devices?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load served by alternating tread devices shall not exceed three.

instruction: What is the maximum opening size allowed in open guards of alternating tread devices?
output: According to NFPA 101, open guards of alternating tread devices shall have rails such that a sphere 21 inches (535 mm) in diameter is not able to pass through any opening.

instruction: What is the maximum percentage of required egress capacity that revolving door openings can be credited for?
output: According to NFPA 101, revolving door openings shall not be given credit for more than 50 percent of the required egress capacity.

instruction: What is the maximum person capacity credited to a revolving door opening?
output: According to NFPA 101, each revolving door opening shall not be credited with more than a 50-person capacity or, if of not less than a 9 ft (2745 mm) diameter, a revolving door assembly shall be permitted egress capacity based on the clear width provided when collapsed into a book-fold position.

instruction: What is the maximum projection allowed within the means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, projections within the means of egress of not more than 4 1/2 in. (114 mm) on each side shall be permitted at a height of 38 in. (965 mm) and below.

instruction: What is the maximum projection for grille hardware markings?
output: According to NFPA 101, grille hardware marking projections shall not be more than 4.5 in. (114 mm) at or below handrail height on each side.

instruction: What is the maximum projection into door opening width on the hinge side that is not considered a reduction?
output: According to NFPA 101, projections of not more than 4 in. (100 mm) into the door opening width on the hinge side shall not be considered reductions in clear width, provided they accommodate panic hardware or fire exit hardware and are located between 34 in. (865 mm) and 48 in. (1220 mm) above the floor.

instruction: What is the maximum projection of a door leaf into the required width of an aisle, corridor, passageway, or landing when fully open?
output: According to NFPA 101, when fully open, any door leaf in a means of egress shall not project more than 7 in. (180 mm) into the required width of an aisle, corridor, passageway, or landing.

instruction: What is the maximum projection of nosing for sloping risers?
output: According to NFPA 101, the projection of the nosing shall not exceed 1 1/2 in. (38 mm) when risers slope under the tread at an angle not to exceed 30 degrees from vertical.

instruction: What is the maximum ratio of depth to height for an alcove where openings below an outside stair require protection?
output: According to NFPA 101, where located in an alcove having a depth that does not exceed one-fourth its height, openings below an outside stair require protection.

instruction: What is the maximum rise for a single ramp run for new ramps?
output: According to NFPA 101, the maximum rise for a single ramp run for new ramps is 30 in. (760 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum riser height for alternating tread devices?
output: According to NFPA 101, the height of the riser for alternating tread devices shall not exceed 9 1/2 in. (240 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum riser height for stairs in new buildings?
output: According to NFPA 101, riser heights shall not exceed 7 in. (180 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum slope for existing ramps?
output: According to NFPA 101, existing ramps shall have a maximum slope of 1 in 8.

instruction: What is the maximum slope for new ramps?
output: According to NFPA 101, new ramps shall have a maximum slope of 1 in 12.

instruction: What is the maximum slope for ramp landings?
output: According to NFPA 101, the slope of the landing shall be not steeper than 1 in 48.

instruction: What is the maximum slope for treads and landings?
output: According to NFPA 101, the tread and landing slope shall not exceed 1/4 in./ft (21 mm/m) (a slope of 1 in 48).

instruction: What is the maximum slope of a walking surface in the direction of travel?
output: According to NFPA 101, the slope of a walking surface in the direction of travel shall not exceed 1 in 20, unless the ramp requirements of 7.2.5 are met.

instruction: What is the maximum slope perpendicular to the direction of travel?
output: According to NFPA 101, the slope perpendicular to the direction of travel shall not exceed 1 in 48.

instruction: What is the maximum spacing for tread construction bars on fire escape stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, tread construction bars on fire escape stairs shall be spaced 1 1/4 inches (32 mm) maximum on centers.

instruction: What is the maximum speed for an existing revolving door assembly with an inside diameter of 10 ft?
input: Component: Revolving Door, Type: Existing, Inside Diameter: 10 ft
output: According to NFPA 101, for an existing revolving door assembly with an inside diameter of 10 ft (3050 mm), the maximum power-driven speed is 7 rpm and the maximum manual speed control is 8 rpm.

instruction: What is the maximum step height permitted below the level of the inside floor in existing buildings?
output: According to NFPA 101, in existing buildings, one step not exceeding 8 in. (205 mm) shall be permitted below the level of the inside floor.

instruction: What is the maximum time new door leaves can remain open when actuated?
output: According to NFPA 101, when actuated, new door leaves remain open for not more than 30 seconds.

instruction: What is the maximum transmitted temperature end point for elevator lobby door assemblies?
output: According to NFPA 101, the transmitted temperature end point for elevator lobby door assemblies shall not exceed 450°F Δ (250°C Δ) above ambient at the end of 30 minutes.

instruction: What is the maximum travel distance to an exit on a story used exclusively for mechanical equipment, furnaces, or boilers with a single means of egress?
input: Occupancy: Mechanical Equipment, Furnaces, or Boilers
output: According to NFPA 101, stories used exclusively for mechanical equipment, furnaces, or boilers shall be permitted to have a single means of egress where the travel distance to an exit on that story is not in excess of the common path of travel limitations of 7.13.1.

instruction: What is the maximum travel distance to the room door for a single means of egress in high-hazard contents areas?
output: According to NFPA 101, a single means of egress is permitted from a high-hazard contents area if rooms or spaces have a travel distance to the room door not exceeding 25 ft (7620 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum variation between the largest and smallest riser or tread depth in any flight?
output: According to NFPA 101, the variation between the sizes of the largest and smallest riser or between the largest and smallest tread depths shall not exceed 3/8 in. (9.5 mm) in any flight.

instruction: What is the maximum variation in the horizontal projection of nosings between adjacent nosings?
output: According to NFPA 101, the variation in the horizontal projection of nosings between adjacent nosings shall not exceed 3/16 in. (4.8 mm).

instruction: What is the maximum variation in the horizontal projection of nosings within a stair flight?
output: According to NFPA 101, the variation in the horizontal projection of all nosings shall not exceed 3/8 in. (9.5 mm) within each stair flight.

instruction: What is the maximum variation in the sizes of adjacent tread depths or riser heights?
output: According to NFPA 101, variation in excess of 1/16 in. (4.8 mm) in the sizes of adjacent tread depths or in the height of adjacent risers shall be prohibited.

instruction: What is the maximum vertical distance for the bottom of new egress markings?
output: According to NFPA 101, the bottom of new egress markings shall be located at a vertical distance of not more than 6 ft (1830 mm) above the top edge of the egress opening.

instruction: What is the maximum vertical drop distance from the step or landing edge for perimeter wall demarcation lines at stairs?
input: Component: Perimeter Wall Demarcation Lines at Stairs
output: According to NFPA 101, at the top or bottom of the stairs, perimeter wall demarcation lines shall drop vertically to the floor within 2 in. (51 mm) of the step or landing edge.

instruction: What is the minimum aggregate width of parallel egress paths formed when revolving door wings are collapsed into the book-fold position?
input: Component: Revolving Door Wings, Condition: Collapsed into Book-Fold Position
output: According to NFPA 101, when revolving door wings are collapsed into the book-fold position, the parallel egress paths formed shall provide an aggregate width of 36 inches (915 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum air discharge rate required for a smokeproof enclosure stair with a dampered relief opening?
output: According to NFPA 101, the stair shall be supplied with sufficient air to discharge at least 2500 ft/min (70.8 m3/min) through the relief opening while maintaining a positive pressure of not less than 0.10 in. water column (25 N/m2) in the stair, relative to the vestibule with all door leaves closed.

instruction: What is the minimum ceiling height difference for a vestibule to serve as a smoke and heat trap?
output: According to NFPA 101, the vestibule ceiling shall be not less than 20 in. (510 mm) higher than the door opening into the vestibule.

instruction: What is the minimum ceiling height for a means of egress in existing buildings?
output: According to NFPA 101, in existing buildings, the ceiling height shall be not less than 7 ft (2135 mm) from the floor, with projections from the ceiling not less than 6 ft 8 in. (2030 mm), with a tolerance of -3/4 in. (-19 mm), above the floor.

instruction: What is the minimum ceiling height for the remaining area of a room or space?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum ceiling height shall be maintained for not less than two-thirds of the ceiling area of any room or space, provided that the ceiling height of the remaining ceiling area is not less than 6 ft 8 in. (2030 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum clear floor area per person for existing bridges serving as horizontal exits?
output: According to NFPA 101, existing bridges serving as horizontal exits shall have sufficient clear floor area to accommodate the occupant load of either connected building or fire area based on 3 ft² (0.28 m²) per person.

instruction: What is the minimum clear floor area required for an occupant evacuation elevator lobby?
output: According to NFPA 101, the elevator lobby clear floor area shall accommodate, at 3 ft² (0.28 m²) per person, a minimum of 25 percent of the occupant load of the floor area served by the lobby.

instruction: What is the minimum clear opening size for access to replacement fire escape stairs via double-hung windows?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum clear opening size for access to replacement fire escape stairs via double-hung windows is 30 inches by 36 inches (760 mm × 915 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum clear width between intermediate handrails?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum clear width between handrails shall be 20 in. (510 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum clear width for a biparting sliding door assembly in emergency breakout mode?
input: Component: Biparting Sliding Door Assembly, Condition: Emergency Breakout Mode
output: According to NFPA 101, a biparting sliding door assembly in emergency breakout mode shall provide a clear opening of not less than 32 inches (810 mm) by all leafs broken out.

instruction: What is the minimum clear width for a door leaf in a two-leaf opening in emergency breakout mode?
input: Component: Door Leaf in Two-Leaf Opening, Condition: Emergency Breakout Mode
output: According to NFPA 101, a door leaf located within a two-leaf opening in emergency breakout mode shall have a clear width of not less than 30 inches (760 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum clear width for a permanently mounted folding or movable partition?
output: According to NFPA 101, permanently mounted folding or movable partitions shall have a clear width of not less than 16.5 inches (420 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum clear width for existing stairs and landings providing egress from an area of refuge?
output: According to NFPA 101, existing stairs and landings that provide a clear width of not less than 37 inches (940 mm), measured at and below handrail height, shall be permitted.

instruction: What is the minimum clear width for occupant evacuation elevator doors?
output: According to NFPA 101, occupant evacuation elevator doors shall be a minimum of 28 in. (710 mm) clear width.

instruction: What is the minimum clear width for turnstiles located in or furnishing access to required exits?
output: According to NFPA 101, turnstiles located in, or furnishing access to, required exits shall provide not less than 16 1/2 in. (420 mm) clear width at and below a height of 39 in. (990 mm) and at least 22 in. (560 mm) clear width at heights above 39 in. (990 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum clear width of a means of egress maintained by wheelchair spaces in an area of refuge?
output: According to NFPA 101, wheelchair spaces shall maintain the width of a means of egress to not less than 36 inches (915 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum clear width of stairs when the occupant load exceeds that permitted by 7.2.2.2.1.2(A)?
input: Condition: Occupant load exceeds that permitted by 7.2.2.2.1.2(A)
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum width clear of all obstructions, except projections not more than 4.5 in. (114 mm) at or below handrail height on each side, shall be as specified in Table 7.2.2.2.1.2(B).

instruction: What is the minimum clear width of stairs when the occupant load is fewer than 50?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum width clear of all obstructions, except projections not more than 4.5 in. (114 mm) at or below handrail height on each side, shall be 36 in. (915 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum clearance between a new handrail and the wall to which it is fastened?
output: According to NFPA 101, new handrails shall be installed to provide a clearance of not less than 2 1/4 in. (57 mm) between the handrail and the wall to which it is fastened.

instruction: What is the minimum design pressure difference required for smokeproof enclosures using pressurization?
output: According to NFPA 101, smokeproof enclosures using pressurization shall have a design pressure difference across the barrier of not less than 0.05 in. water column (12.5 N/m2) in sprinklered buildings.

instruction: What is the minimum dimension for a landing in a new building?
output: According to NFPA 101, every landing in a new building shall have a dimension, measured in the direction of travel, that is not less than the width of the stair.

instruction: What is the minimum dimension of a vestibule used in a smokeproof enclosure?
output: According to NFPA 101, every vestibule shall have a minimum dimension of not less than the required width of the corridor leading to it and a dimension of not less than 6 ft (1830 mm) in the direction of travel.

instruction: What is the minimum distance at which a directional indicator must be identifiable?
output: According to NFPA 101, the directional indicator shall be identifiable as a directional indicator at a distance of 40 ft (12 m).

instruction: What is the minimum distance between a fire escape stair component and an opening that requires fire door or fire window assemblies?
input: Component: Fire Escape Stairs, Condition: Opening horizontally within 15 ft (4570 mm)
output: According to NFPA 101, fire door or fire window assemblies are required where the opening or any portion of the opening is located horizontally within 15 ft (4570 mm) of any balcony, platform, or stairway constituting a component of the fire escape stair.

instruction: What is the minimum distance between the alternating tread device handrail and any other object?
output: According to NFPA 101, a distance of not less than 6 in. (150 mm) shall be provided between the alternating tread device handrail and any other object.

instruction: What is the minimum distance for floor level changes on each side of a door opening?
output: According to NFPA 101, floor level changes on each side of a door opening shall be for a distance not less than the width of the widest leaf and, for other than existing installations, not less than 36 inches (915 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum distance for which outside walls must be protected adjacent to a horizontal exit?
output: According to NFPA 101, outside walls shall be protected for a distance of 10 ft (3050 mm) on each side of the horizontal exit.

instruction: What is the minimum distance from the EXIT legend for a directional indicator?
output: According to NFPA 101, the directional indicator shall be located outside of the EXIT legend, not less than 3/8 in. (9.5 mm) from any letter.

instruction: What is the minimum distance that a revolving door assembly must be located from the foot or top of stairs or escalators?
input: Component: Revolving Door Assembly, Condition: Proximity to Stairs or Escalators
output: According to NFPA 101, revolving door assemblies shall not be used within 10 feet (3050 mm) of the foot or the top of stairs or escalators.

instruction: What is the minimum duration for a manual release device to remain in the open position?
input: Component: Security access turnstile manual release device
output: According to NFPA 101, the manual release device shall remain in the open position for not less than 30 seconds.

instruction: What is the minimum duration of continuous illumination required for exit enclosures with photoluminescent materials prior to occupancy?
input: Component: Exit Stair with Photoluminescent Materials
output: According to NFPA 101, the exit enclosure shall be continuously illuminated for at least 60 minutes prior to periods when the building is occupied.

instruction: What is the minimum duration of operation for an elevator used as a second means of egress in a fire event?
input: Component: Elevator used as second means of egress
output: According to NFPA 101, an elevator used as a second means of egress shall be protected to ensure a minimum 1 hour of operation in the event of a fire.

instruction: What is the minimum elevation difference that requires a ramp or stair in a means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, changes in level in a means of egress where the elevation difference exceeds 21 in. (535 mm) shall be achieved by a ramp or stair.

instruction: What is the minimum fire protection rating for elevator lobby door assemblies?
output: According to NFPA 101, elevator lobby door assemblies shall have a minimum 1-hour fire protection rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire protection rating for openings in barriers separating an area of refuge from the remainder of the story?
output: According to NFPA 101, openings in barriers separating an area of refuge from the remainder of the story shall have not less than a 20-minute fire protection rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire protection rating for the door opening into the vestibule and from the vestibule to the smokeproof enclosure?
output: According to NFPA 101, the door opening into the vestibule shall be protected with an approved fire door assembly having a minimum 1 1/2-hour fire protection rating, and the fire door assembly from the vestibule to the smokeproof enclosure shall have a minimum 20-minute fire protection rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire protection rating required for a door assembly to a smokeproof enclosure with natural ventilation via an open exterior balcony?
input: Component: Door Assembly to Smokeproof Enclosure
output: According to NFPA 101, where access to the enclosure is by means of an open exterior balcony, the door assembly to the enclosure shall have a minimum 1 1/2-hour fire protection rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire protection rating required for openings below an outside stair?
output: According to NFPA 101, openings below an outside stair shall be protected with an assembly having a minimum 3/4-hour fire protection rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire resistance rating for an existing barrier separating an area of refuge from the remainder of the story?
output: According to NFPA 101, an existing barrier separating an area of refuge from the remainder of the story shall have a minimum 30-minute fire resistance rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire resistance rating for an exit separation connecting four or more stories?
output: According to NFPA 101, the separation shall have a minimum 2-hour fire resistance rating where the exit connects four or more stories, unless one of the specified conditions exists.

instruction: What is the minimum fire resistance rating for barriers forming an elevator lobby?
output: According to NFPA 101, barriers forming the elevator lobby shall have a minimum 1-hour fire resistance rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire resistance rating for exit access corridors serving an area with an occupant load exceeding 30?
input: Component: Exit Access Corridors, Condition: Occupant Load Exceeding 30
output: According to NFPA 101, corridors used as exit access and serving an area having an occupant load exceeding 30 shall be separated from other parts of the building by walls having not less than a 1-hour fire resistance rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire resistance rating for exit stair enclosures in existing buildings protected throughout by an automatic sprinkler system?
input: Building Type: Existing, Condition: Protected Throughout by Automatic Sprinkler System
output: According to NFPA 101, existing exit stair enclosures in existing buildings protected throughout by an automatic sprinkler system shall have a minimum 1-hour fire resistance rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire resistance rating for one of the outside walls adjacent to a horizontal exit?
input: Condition: One outside wall within 10 ft (3050 mm) of horizontal exit
output: According to NFPA 101, one of the outside walls within 10 ft (3050 mm) from intersection with the horizontal exit shall have a 2-hour fire resistance rating with opening protectives having a minimum 1 1/2-hour fire protection rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire resistance rating for the separation required by 7.1.3.2.1(3)?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum 2-hour fire-resistance-rated separation required by 7.1.3.2.1(3) shall be constructed of an assembly of noncombustible or limited-combustible materials and shall be supported by construction having a minimum 2-hour fire resistance rating.

instruction: What is the minimum fire-resistance rating for elevator machine/control rooms and machinery/control spaces associated with occupant evacuation elevators?
input: Component: Elevator machine/control rooms and machinery/control spaces
output: According to NFPA 101, elevator machine/control rooms and machinery/control spaces associated with occupant evacuation elevators shall be separated from all building areas, other than elevator hoistways, by a minimum 2-hour fire-resistance-rated construction.

instruction: What is the minimum fire-resistance rating for shaft system walls separating the enclosed exit stair from the remainder of the building?
input: Component: Shaft system walls separating enclosed exit stair from building
output: According to NFPA 101, the shaft system walls separating the enclosed exit stair from the remainder of the building shall have a minimum 2-hour fire resistance rating and minimum 1.5-hour fire-protection-rated opening protectives.

instruction: What is the minimum fire-resistance rating for wiring providing normal power, standby power, control signals, communication, lighting, heating, air-conditioning, ventilation, and fire detecting systems to occupant evacuation elevators?
input: Component: Wiring for occupant evacuation elevator systems
output: According to NFPA 101, wires or cables providing normal power, standby power, control signals, communication, lighting, heating, air-conditioning, ventilation, and fire detecting systems to occupant evacuation elevators shall be protected by one of the following: (1) Type CI cable with a minimum 2-hour fire resistance rating, (2) enclosed in a minimum 2-hour fire-resistance-rated construction, or (3) wiring approved as providing a 2-hour performance alternative.

instruction: What is the minimum headroom for new stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum headroom for new stairs is 6 feet 8 inches (2030 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum headroom for replacement fire escape stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum headroom for replacement fire escape stairs is 6 feet 8 inches (2030 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum headroom for stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum headroom is 6 ft 8 in. (2030 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum headroom in a means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, means of egress shall provide headroom of not less than 7 ft 6 in. (2285 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum headroom on stairs and stair landings?
output: According to NFPA 101, headroom on stairs and stair landings shall be not less than 6 ft 8 in. (2030 mm) and shall be measured vertically above a plane parallel to, and tangent with, the most forward projection of the stair tread.

instruction: What is the minimum headroom requirement along a designated means of egress path within normally unoccupied building service equipment support areas?
output: According to NFPA 101, where a means of egress path is required, minimum headroom shall be 6 ft 8 in. (2030 mm) along the entire designated means of egress path.

instruction: What is the minimum height above floor for projections that are not considered reductions in clear width?
output: According to NFPA 101, projections exceeding 6 ft 8 in. (2030 mm) above the floor shall not be considered reductions in clear width.

instruction: What is the minimum height above floor that requires guards at open sides of means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, guards shall be provided at open sides of means of egress that exceed 30 in. (760 mm) above the floor or finished ground level below.

instruction: What is the minimum height for an emergency exit symbol applied on a door?
output: According to NFPA 101, the emergency exit symbol applied on the door shall be a minimum of 4 in. (100 mm) in height.

instruction: What is the minimum height for an opaque visual obstruction on fire escape stairs?
input: Component: Fire Escape Stairs, Condition: Height more than 36 ft (11 m) above finished ground level
output: According to NFPA 101, fire escape stairs more than 36 ft (11 m) above the finished ground level shall be provided with an opaque visual obstruction not less than 48 in. (1220 mm) in height.

instruction: What is the minimum height for an opaque visual obstruction on outside ramps?
input: Component: Outside Ramp, Condition: Height more than 36 ft (11 m) above finished ground level
output: According to NFPA 101, outside ramps more than 36 ft (11 m) above the finished ground level shall be provided with an opaque visual obstruction not less than 48 in. (1220 mm) in height.

instruction: What is the minimum height for curbs or barriers?
output: According to NFPA 101, curbs or barriers shall be not less than 4 in. (100 mm) in height.

instruction: What is the minimum height for existing guards on existing stairs?
input: Component: Guards, Condition: Existing, Component: Stairs
output: According to NFPA 101, existing guards on existing stairs shall be permitted to be not less than 30 in. (760 mm) high.

instruction: What is the minimum height for existing guards within dwelling units?
input: Component: Guards, Condition: Existing, Occupancy: Dwelling units
output: According to NFPA 101, existing guards within dwelling units shall be permitted to be not less than 36 in. (915 mm) high.

instruction: What is the minimum height for floor level numbers on stairway identification signs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the floor level number shall be located below the stairway identifier in minimum 5 in. (125 mm) high numbers.

instruction: What is the minimum height for guards?
output: According to NFPA 101, guards shall be not less than 42 in. (1065 mm) high.

instruction: What is the minimum height of an opaque visual obstruction for outside stairs more than 36 ft above finished ground level?
output: According to NFPA 101, outside stairs more than 36 ft (11 m) above the finished ground level shall be provided with an opaque visual obstruction not less than 48 in. (1220 mm) in height.

instruction: What is the minimum height of risers for new stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum height of risers for new stairs is 4 inches (100 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum horizontal extension of a fire barrier for a bridge serving as a horizontal exit?
input: Component: Bridge serving horizontal exit between buildings
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum 2-hour fire-resistance-rated barrier for a bridge serving as a horizontal exit shall extend horizontally for not less than 10 ft (3050 mm) to each side of the bridge.

instruction: What is the minimum horizontal extension of a new handrail beyond the top riser?
input: Component: Handrail, Condition: New, Occupancy: Other than dwelling units
output: According to NFPA 101, new handrails that are not continuous between flights shall extend horizontally not less than 12 in. (305 mm) beyond the top riser.

instruction: What is the minimum illumination level for externally illuminated signs?
output: According to NFPA 101, externally illuminated signs shall be illuminated by not less than 5 foot-candles (54 lux) at the illuminated surface and shall have a contrast ratio of not less than 0.5.

instruction: What is the minimum illumination level for floors and other walking surfaces, other than new stairs, during conditions of stair use?
input: Component: Floors and Walking Surfaces (excluding new stairs), Condition: Stair Use
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum illumination for floors and other walking surfaces, other than new stairs during conditions of stair use, shall be at least 1 foot-candle (10.8 lux), measured at the floor.

instruction: What is the minimum illumination level for walking surfaces of exit access in assembly occupancies during periods of performances or projections involving directed light?
input: Occupancy: Assembly, Condition: Performances or Projections with Directed Light
output: According to NFPA 101, in assembly occupancies, the illumination of the walking surfaces of exit access shall be at least 0.2 foot-candle (2.2 lux) during periods of performances or projections involving directed light.

instruction: What is the minimum illumination level permitted for emergency lighting at the end of 1.5 hours?
input: Component: Emergency Lighting, Condition: After 1.5 Hours
output: According to NFPA 101, illumination levels shall be permitted to decline to not less than an average of 0.6 foot-candle (6.5 lux) and, at any point, not less than 0.06 foot-candle (0.65 lux) at the end of 1.5 hours.

instruction: What is the minimum illumination level required for dimmable lighting control devices in exit enclosures?
output: According to NFPA 101, lighting control devices that dim the lighting levels within the exit enclosure shall provide a minimum of 1 ft-candle (10.8 lux) of illumination measured at the walking surface.

instruction: What is the minimum illumination of means of egress along the required path?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum illumination of means of egress along the required path shall be 0.2 foot-candle (2.2 lux).

instruction: What is the minimum initial illumination level required for emergency lighting along the path of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, emergency lighting facilities shall provide initial illumination that is not less than an average of 1 foot-candle (10.8 lux) and, at any point, not less than 0.1 foot-candle (1.1 lux), measured along the path of egress at floor level.

instruction: What is the minimum length for ramp landings in the direction of travel?
output: According to NFPA 101, every landing, except as otherwise provided, shall be not less than 60 in. (1525 mm) long in the direction of travel, unless the landing is an approved existing landing.

instruction: What is the minimum length for ramp landings not part of an accessible route?
input: Component: Ramp Landings, Condition: Not part of accessible route
output: According to NFPA 101, where the ramp is not part of an accessible route, the ramp landings shall not be required to exceed 48 in. (1220 mm) in the direction of travel.

instruction: What is the minimum length of the actuating portion of a cross bar or push pad on a door leaf?
output: According to NFPA 101, the actuating portion of the cross bar or push pad shall extend not less than one-half of the width of the door leaf measured from the latch stile.

instruction: What is the minimum letter height for a sign on a door that remains unlocked?
output: According to NFPA 101, doors that remain unlocked when the building or space is occupied shall be marked with a readily visible, durable sign in letters not less than 1 in. (25 mm) high on a contrasting background.

instruction: What is the minimum letter height for a sign on the egress side of a door?
input: Component: Sign on Egress Side of Door
output: According to NFPA 101, a readily visible, durable sign on the egress side of each door shall have letters not less than 1 inch (25 mm) high on a contrasting background.

instruction: What is the minimum letter height for elevator signs in a means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, elevator signs in a means of egress shall have a minimum letter height of 5/8 in. (16 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum letter height for existing exit signs?
output: According to NFPA 101, for existing signs, the required wording shall be permitted to be in plainly legible letters not less than 4 in. (100 mm) high.

instruction: What is the minimum letter height for identification of the lower and upper terminus of a stairway?
output: According to NFPA 101, identification of the lower and upper terminus of the stairway shall be on the sign in minimum 1 in. (25 mm) high letters or numbers.

instruction: What is the minimum letter height for the word 'EXIT' on an exit sign?
output: According to NFPA 101, the word 'EXIT' on an exit sign shall be in letters not less than 1 in. (25 mm) high.

instruction: What is the minimum letter width for the word EXIT?
output: According to NFPA 101, the word EXIT shall be in letters of a width not less than 2 in. (51 mm), except the letter I, and the minimum spacing between letters shall be not less than 3/8 in. (9.5 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum number of means of egress for existing buildings with an occupant load more than 1000?
output: According to NFPA 101, for existing buildings with an occupant load more than 1000, the number of means of egress shall be not less than 4.

instruction: What is the minimum projected tread depth for alternating tread devices?
output: According to NFPA 101, treads for alternating tread devices shall have a projected tread depth of not less than 5 2/3 in. (145 mm), with each tread providing 9 1/2 in. (240 mm) of depth including tread overlap.

instruction: What is the minimum radius for graspable edges of a handrail?
output: According to NFPA 101, graspable edges of handrails shall be rounded to provide a radius of not less than 0.125 in. (3.2 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum required clear width of a door opening serving as the sole exit discharge from a stairway?
input: Component: Stairway, Condition: Door serves as sole exit discharge
output: According to NFPA 101, where a door assembly serves as the sole means of exit discharge from a stairway, the clear width of the door opening shall be not less than two-thirds the required width of the stairway.

instruction: What is the minimum separation distance for exits in buildings protected throughout by an approved, supervised automatic sprinkler system?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum separation distance for exits in buildings protected throughout by an approved, supervised automatic sprinkler system shall be not less than one-third the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the building or area.

instruction: What is the minimum stair width for a total cumulative occupant load assigned to the stair of 2000 persons or more?
input: Condition: Total cumulative occupant load ≥ 2000 persons
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum stair width is 56 in. (1420 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum stair width for a total cumulative occupant load assigned to the stair of less than 2000 persons?
input: Condition: Total cumulative occupant load < 2000 persons
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum stair width is 44 in. (1120 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum tenable condition duration required for an area of refuge not exceeding 1000 square feet?
input: Condition: Area of Refuge ≤ 1000 sq ft
output: According to NFPA 101, for any area of refuge that does not exceed 1000 square feet (93 square meters) of clear floor area, it shall be demonstrated by calculation or test that tenable conditions are maintained within the area of refuge for a period of 15 minutes.

instruction: What is the minimum tread depth for a spiral stairway?
output: According to NFPA 101, treads shall have a depth not less than 7 1/2 in. (190 mm) at a point 12 in. (305 mm) from the narrower edge.

instruction: What is the minimum tread depth for a stair used to accommodate a change in level?
output: According to NFPA 101, where a stair is used to accommodate a change in level, the tread depth shall be not less than 13 in. (330 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum tread depth for existing curved stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, existing curved stairs shall have a tread depth of not less than 10 in. (255 mm) at a point 12 in. (305 mm) from the narrower end of the tread and the smallest radius is not less than twice the stair width.

instruction: What is the minimum tread depth for new stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum tread depth for new stairs is 11 inches (280 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum tread depth for new winders?
output: According to NFPA 101, new winders shall have a tread depth of not less than 6 in. (150 mm) and a tread depth of not less than 11 in. (280 mm) at a point 12 in. (305 mm) from the narrowest edge.

instruction: What is the minimum tread depth for stairs in new buildings?
output: According to NFPA 101, the stairway shall have a tread depth of not less than 11 in. (280 mm) for a portion of the stairway width sufficient to provide egress capacity for the occupant load served.

instruction: What is the minimum tread depth for stairs?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum tread depth is 9 in. (230 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum width and direction of travel dimension for a vestibule?
output: According to NFPA 101, vestibules shall have a dimension of not less than 44 in. (1120 mm) in width and not less than 6 ft (1830 mm) in the direction of travel.

instruction: What is the minimum width for a new bridge?
output: According to NFPA 101, every bridge shall be not less than the width of the door opening to which it leads and shall be not less than 44 in. (1120 mm) wide for new construction.

instruction: What is the minimum width for an egress component where no specific minimum is specified?
output: According to NFPA 101, where another part of this chapter and Chapters 11 through 43 do not specify a minimum width, the minimum width shall be not less than 36 in. (915 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum width for existing exit discharge paths to a public way?
output: According to NFPA 101, existing exit discharge paths to a public way shall have a width of not less than 28 in. (710 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum width for existing ramps?
output: According to NFPA 101, existing ramps shall have a minimum width of 30 in. (760 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum width for exit access serving not more than six people and having a length not exceeding 50 ft?
output: According to NFPA 101, the width shall be not less than 18 in. (455 mm) at and below a height of 38 in. (965 mm), and not less than 28 in. (710 mm) above a height of 38 in. (965 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum width for new exit access?
output: According to NFPA 101, a width of not less than 36 in. (915 mm) for new exit access shall be capable of being provided without moving permanent walls.

instruction: What is the minimum width for ramp landings?
output: According to NFPA 101, every landing shall have a width not less than the width of the ramp.

instruction: What is the minimum width of an exit access leading to an exit?
output: According to NFPA 101, the width of an exit access leading to an exit shall be not less than the required capacity of the exit to which it leads.

instruction: What is the minimum width of an exit passageway into which an exit stair discharges or that serves as a horizontal transfer within an exit stair system?
output: According to NFPA 101, the minimum width of the exit passageway shall be not less than the minimum width of any exit.

instruction: What is the minimum width of an opening for curtains to be considered as not obstructing means of egress?
output: According to NFPA 101, curtains are installed across an opening that is at least 6 ft (1830 mm) in width.

instruction: What is the minimum width of exit access in existing buildings?
output: According to NFPA 101, in existing buildings, the width of exit access shall be permitted to be not less than 28 in. (710 mm).

instruction: What is the minimum width of the marking stripe on panic hardware for exit enclosures?
output: According to NFPA 101, where panic hardware is installed, the marking stripe shall have a minimum width of 1 in. (25 mm) and be applied to the entire length of the actuating bar or touch pad.

instruction: What is the mounting height range for an exit sign?
output: According to NFPA 101, the bottom of the exit sign shall be not less than 6 in. (150 mm) but not more than 18 in. (455 mm) above the floor.

instruction: What is the mounting height range for new installations of cross bars or push pads on door leaves?
output: According to NFPA 101, new installations of cross bars or push pads shall be mounted not less than 34 in. (865 mm) and not more than 48 in. (1220 mm) above the floor.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for airport traffic control tower observation levels?
input: Occupancy: Airport Traffic Control Tower Observation Levels
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for airport traffic control tower observation levels is 40 gross square feet (3.7 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for apartment buildings?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for apartment buildings is 200 gross square feet (18.6 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for bench-type seating?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for bench-type seating is 1 person per 18 linear inches (455 linear mm).

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for board and care, large?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for board and care, large is 200 gross square feet (18.6 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for business use areas?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for Business Use (other than concentrated) is 150 ft² (14 m²) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for casinos and similar gaming areas?
input: Occupancy: Casinos and similar gaming areas
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for casinos and similar gaming areas is 11 ft² (1 m²) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for collaboration rooms or spaces greater than 450 square feet (41.8 square meters) in area?
input: Occupancy: Collaboration Rooms/Spaces >450 ft² (41.8 m²) in Area
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for collaboration rooms or spaces greater than 450 square feet (41.8 square meters) in area is 15 gross square feet (1.4 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for day-care use?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for day-care use is 35 net square feet (3.3 net square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for floors or portions used only for storage, receiving, and shipping, not open to general public?
input: Occupancy: Storage, Receiving, and Shipping (Not Open to General Public)
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for floors or portions used only for storage, receiving, and shipping, and not open to general public is 300 gross square feet (27.9 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for general- and high-hazard industrial use?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for general- and high-hazard industrial use is 100 gross square feet (9.3 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for lighting and access catwalks, galleries, and gridirons?
input: Occupancy: Lighting and access catwalks, galleries, gridirons
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for lighting and access catwalks, galleries, and gridirons is 100 net ft² (9.3 net m²) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for mercantile sales area on floors above street floor?
input: Occupancy: Mercantile, Sales Area on Floors Above Street Floor
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for mercantile sales area on floors above street floor is 60 gross square feet (5.6 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for mercantile sales area on two or more street floors?
input: Occupancy: Mercantile, Sales Area on Two or More Street Floors
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for mercantile sales area on two or more street floors is 40 gross square feet (3.7 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for residential hotels and dormitories?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for residential hotels and dormitories is 200 gross square feet (18.6 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for skating rinks?
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for skating rinks is 50 ft² (4.6 m²) per person.

instruction: What is the occupant load factor for storage in other than storage and mercantile occupancies?
input: Occupancy: Storage in Other Than Storage and Mercantile Occupancies
output: According to NFPA 101, the occupant load factor for storage in other than storage and mercantile occupancies is 500 gross square feet (46.5 square meters) per person.

instruction: What is the permitted variation in height for a bottom or top riser adjoining a sloping public way?
input: Condition: Bottom or top riser adjoins a sloping public way, walk, or driveway
output: According to NFPA 101, the bottom or top riser shall be permitted to have a variation in height of not more than 1 in. in every 12 in. (25 mm in every 305 mm) of stairway width.

instruction: What is the reduced collapsing force for revolving door assemblies under specific conditions?
input: Condition: Power failure, sprinkler actuation, smoke detection, or manual control
output: According to NFPA 101, the collapsing force for revolving door assemblies shall be reduced to a force not to exceed 130 lbf (580 N) under conditions of power failure, actuation of automatic sprinkler system, actuation of a smoke detection system within 75 ft (23 m) of the revolving door assemblies, or actuation of a manual control switch.

instruction: What is the required air change rate and exhaust percentage for a vestibule?
output: According to NFPA 101, the vestibule shall be provided with not less than one air change per minute, and the exhaust shall be 150 percent of the supply.

instruction: What is the required capacity of means of egress from a point of convergence where means of egress from a story above and a story below converge at an intermediate story?
output: According to NFPA 101, where means of egress from a story above and a story below converge at an intermediate story, the capacity of the means of egress from the point of convergence shall be not less than the sum of the required capacity of the two means of egress.

instruction: What is the required capacity of means of egress when more than one means of egress is required?
output: According to NFPA 101, where more than one means of egress is required, the means of egress shall be of such width and capacity that the loss of any one means of egress leaves available not less than 50 percent of the required capacity.

instruction: What is the required clear width between handrails for alternating tread devices?
output: According to NFPA 101, the clear width between handrails for alternating tread devices shall be not less than 17 in. (430 mm) and not more than 24 in. (610 mm).

instruction: What is the required guard height range for alternating tread devices?
output: According to NFPA 101, alternating tread device guards, with a top rail that also serves as a handrail, shall have a height of not less than 30 in. (760 mm), and not more than 34 in. (865 mm).

instruction: What is the required handrail perimeter dimension for a non-circular shape?
output: According to NFPA 101, handrails with a shape other than circular shall have a perimeter dimension of not less than 4 in. (100 mm) and not more than 6.25 in. (160 mm), with the largest cross-sectional dimension not more than 2.25 in. (57 mm).

instruction: What is the required horizontal distance for building enclosure walls exposed to nonrated stairway walls?
input: Component: Stairway, Condition: Nonrated walls or unprotected openings
output: According to NFPA 101, building enclosure walls within 10 ft (3050 mm) horizontally of the nonrated wall or unprotected opening shall be constructed as required for stairway enclosures.

instruction: What is the required mounting height range for surface-mounted latch release hardware on a door leaf?
output: According to NFPA 101, surface-mounted latch release hardware on the door leaf shall be mounted not less than 34 in. (865 mm) and not more than 48 in. (1220 mm) above the floor.

instruction: What is the required size for a wheelchair space in an area of refuge?
output: According to NFPA 101, each area of refuge shall be sized to accommodate one wheelchair space of 30 inches by 48 inches (760 mm by 1220 mm) for every 200 occupants, or portion thereof.

instruction: What is the required wheelchair space size in an elevator lobby for evacuation?
output: According to NFPA 101, the elevator lobby clear floor area shall accommodate one wheelchair space of 30 in. × 48 in. (760 mm × 1220 mm) for each 50 persons, or portion thereof, of the occupant load of the floor area served by the lobby.

instruction: What is the requirement for wheelchair spaces in an occupant evacuation elevator lobby?
output: According to NFPA 101, the elevator lobby clear floor area shall accommodate one wheelchair space of 30 in. × 48 in. (760 mm × 1220 mm) for each 50 persons, or portion thereof, of the occupant load of the floor area served by the lobby.

instruction: What is the vertical extent of fire resistance rating required for separation from stairs?
input: Component: Stairs, Condition: Nonrated walls or unprotected openings
output: According to NFPA 101, the fire resistance rating of the separation extending 10 ft (3050 mm) from the stairs shall not be required to extend from finished ground level to a point 10 ft (3050 mm) above the topmost landing or to the roofline, whichever is lower.

instruction: How is the available egress width reduced when a pair of intermediate handrails are provided within the stairway width?
output: According to IBC, where a pair of intermediate handrails are provided within the stairway width without a walking surface between them and the distance between the pair is greater than 6 inches (152 mm), the available egress width shall be reduced by the distance between the closest edges of each such intermediate pair of handrails that is greater than 6 inches (152 mm).

instruction: How is the minimum clear width between rows increased for additional seats beyond 21 in dual-access rows?
input: Component: Seating Row, Condition: Dual Access, Seats without Backrests
output: According to IBC, the minimum clear width of 12 inches (305 mm) between rows shall be increased by 0.3 inch (7.6 mm) for every additional seat beyond 21 where seats are without backrests.

instruction: What are the clear width requirements for gaps or breaks in discontinuous mid-aisle handrails?
output: According to IBC, gaps or breaks in discontinuous mid-aisle handrails shall have a clear width of not less than 22 inches (559 mm) and not greater than 36 inches (914 mm), measured horizontally.

instruction: What are the construction tolerances for risers of unequal height on stepped aisles?
input: Component: Stepped aisle risers, Condition: Unequal height
output: According to IBC, where stepped aisle treads are less than 22 inches (560 mm) in depth, each riser of unequal height shall not be more than 3/8 inch (9.5 mm) in height different from adjacent risers. Where treads are 22 inches (560 mm) or greater in depth, the difference shall not exceed 3/4 inch (19.1 mm).

instruction: What are the curvature or bevel limits for nosing on stair treads?
output: According to IBC, nosings shall have a curvature or bevel of not less than 1/16 inch (1.6 mm) but not more than 9/16 inch (14.3 mm) from the foremost projection of the tread.

instruction: What are the dimensional requirements for Type II handrails?
output: According to IBC, Type II handrails with a perimeter greater than 6 1/4 inches (160 mm) shall provide a graspable finger recess area on both sides of the profile. The finger recess shall begin within a distance of 3/4 inch (19 mm) measured vertically from the tallest portion of the profile and achieve a depth of not less than 5/16 inch (8 mm) within 7/8 inch (22 mm) below the widest portion of the profile. This required depth shall continue for not less than 3/8 inch (10 mm) to a level that is not less than 1 3/4 inches (45 mm) below the tallest portion of the profile. The width of the handrail above the recess shall be not less than 1 1/4 inches (32 mm) to not greater than 2 3/4 inches (70 mm). Edges shall have a minimum radius of 0.01 inch (0.25 mm).

instruction: What are the guard requirements for mechanical equipment, systems, and devices located within 10 feet of a roof edge or open side?
input: Condition: Mechanical equipment, systems, and devices within 10 feet of roof edge or open side; Walking surface more than 30 inches above floor/roof/grade
output: According to IBC, guards shall be provided where various components that require service are located within 10 feet (3048 mm) of a roof edge or open side of a walking surface and such edge or open side is located more than 30 inches (762 mm) above the floor, roof or grade below. The guard shall extend not less than 30 inches (762 mm) beyond each end of such components. The guard shall be constructed so as to prevent the passage of a sphere 21 inches (533 mm) in diameter.

instruction: What are the height requirements for a handhold adjacent to a stairway with not more than two risers?
input: Condition: Platform lift stationary, stairway with not more than two risers
output: According to IBC, the handhold shall be located not less than 34 inches (864 mm) and not more than 42 inches (1067 mm) above the bottom landing of the stairway.

instruction: What are the height requirements for the lowest edge of a sign mounted between posts or pylons with clear distance greater than 12 inches?
output: According to IBC, where a sign or other obstruction is mounted between posts or pylons and the clear distance between the posts or pylons is greater than 12 inches (305 mm), the lowest edge of such sign or obstruction shall be 27 inches (686 mm) maximum or 80 inches (2032 mm) minimum above the finished floor or ground.

instruction: What are the maximum and minimum riser heights for stairways?
output: According to IBC, stair riser heights shall be 7 inches (178 mm) maximum and 4 inches (102 mm) minimum.

instruction: What are the maximum exit access travel distances for various occupancies with and without a sprinkler system?
input: Occupancy: A, E, F-1, M, R, S-1
output: According to IBC, for Occupancy A, E, F-1, M, R, S-1, the maximum exit access travel distance without a sprinkler system is 200 feet, and with a sprinkler system is 250 feet.

instruction: What are the maximum opening sizes for guards at the end of aisles in assembly seating areas?
input: Occupancy: Assembly seating; Condition: Guards at end of aisles
output: According to IBC, in assembly seating areas, guards required at the end of aisles shall not have openings that allow passage of a sphere 4 inches (102 mm) in diameter up to a height of 26 inches (660 mm), and from a height of 26 inches (660 mm) to 42 inches (1067 mm) above the adjacent walking surfaces, guards shall not have openings that allow passage of a sphere 8 inches (203 mm) in diameter.

instruction: What are the maximum riser height and minimum tread depth for Group R-3, R-2 dwelling units, and accessory Group U occupancies?
input: Occupancy: Group R-3, Group R-2 dwelling units, Group U accessory to Group R-3 or R-2
output: According to IBC, the maximum riser height shall be 7 3/4 inches (197 mm); the minimum tread depth shall be 10 inches (254 mm); the minimum winder tread depth at the walkline shall be 10 inches (254 mm); and the minimum winder tread depth shall be 6 inches (152 mm).

instruction: What are the maximum riser height and minimum tread depth for stairways in Group I-3 facilities serving guard towers, observation stations, and control rooms?
input: Occupancy: Group I-3, Area: not more than 250 square feet (23 m2)
output: According to IBC, stairways shall be permitted to have a maximum riser height of 8 inches (203 mm) and a minimum tread depth of 9 inches (229 mm).

instruction: What are the minimum illumination levels for emergency lighting under emergency power?
output: According to IBC, emergency lighting facilities shall be arranged to provide initial illumination that is not less than an average of 1 footcandle (11 lux) and a minimum at any point of 0.1 footcandle (1 lux) measured along the path of egress at floor level.
